claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gunplay as responsive with crisp movement mechanics, though landing after a jump feels less smooth.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Bomb Has Been Defused[/h1]

[b][u]PROS[/u]:[/b]  Counter-Strike: Source is one of the oldest active FPS titles available that still sees a regular player base.  It's gunplay still feels responsive & the controls still have that smooth feel to them save for landing after a jump.  The goals are simple, as is the gun & equipment buying mechanic at the start of each round.  Teams can give commands if lacking a microphone, allowing other teammates to collaborate while on the move.  It's basic feel does have an air of nostalgia to it, keeping things as simple as possible.  The guns all have that kick to them, with their sounds as well as the sound of footsteps being one of the few reliable ways of tracking targets.  The visuals are what one could expect of a game built on the source engine, nothing too special, but polished enough to know what's going on.

[b][u]CONS[/u]:[/b]  Although the game still functions how it's intended to, time is not so kind.  Though there's not that much wrong with it, it lacks a great deal of polish & content that other games have built on.  Built on is the key word there, as this title could be seen as one of the titles used as the formula for many shooters enjoyed today.  Is it fair to judge a title that is over two decades old?  No, but it is a comparison that is forced upon it.  It's age becomes the only real downside of the title.

[b][u]ACHIEVEMENTS[/u]:[/b]  This list has a few surprising snags.  Besides the standard grind based achievements, the majority can be done by using bots.  Some, such as The Road To Hell, may be a challenge, but the bots do have the potential to help clear out the bulk of the list.  The exceptions are Dressed To Kill, Friendly Attire, & Clan Warfare. claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features custom community modes and servers including surf, bunny hopping, zombie hunter, jailbreak, and TTT.

citations.review_text: The best New installment of the counter strike series. surf
This is the best community game I've ever played, the amount of unique community run servers cannot be understated, from Surf and Bunny Hopping to Deathrun and WarcraftCS, this game has it all.
Incredibly fun, Jailbreak and TTT community still active after so long

Counter-Strike: Source is one of those games that's still fun no matter how old it gets. The Source engine gives it a lot of charm, and the huge amount of mods, custom maps, and community servers means there's always something different to play. I also appreciate the little details, like voice chat changing based on where players are, which makes the game feel more alive. And unlike a lot of modern shooters, there are no paid skins, battle passes, or cosmetic shops everywhere—it's just a solid game that's all about having fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game does not demand high-end computer hardware to run.

citations.review_text:
Why play this edition of Counter-Strike over CS:1.6, CS:CZ(?), CS"GO or CS:2?
Difficult to say for someone who grew up playing this game on a net cafe...
Most of us play this game to let off steam from a hard day.  I stopped playing on normal gamemode servers years ago, I now only spend my time in Zombie hunter and poolday servers.  It's a weirdly relaxing experience.  The physics objects greatly enhance the experience and the moddability of the game make sure shooting never gets boring.

I reckon most machines can run this game by now so the only thing holding you back from playing this is probably the price.
Get this game from a resaler or wait for a steam sale, else you shouldn't buy it at the current price (20Euros).
Excellent game! I strongly recommend to anyone who likes a good online fps. It doesn't require a state of art computer and the graphics are more than decent. Hours of fun ahead!!!
